title: Sending JSON and status codes
summary: Answer with res.json and choose the right status code with res.status and res.sendStatus.

quiz.q: Which status code means "the thing you asked for was created"?
quiz.explain: 201 Created is the usual answer to a successful POST that adds something. 200 is plain success, 301 is a redirect and 404 means not found.

quiz.q: Complete the line so the server answers with status 404 and a JSON message.
quiz.explain: `res.status(404)` sets the code and returns `res`, so you can chain `.json(...)` straight after it.

quiz.q: What status does a route send if you only call `res.json({ ok: true })` and never set one?
quiz.explain: The default status is 200 (OK). You only need `res.status(...)` when you want a different one.

quiz.q: Put the lines in order to build a route that answers a POST with 201 and JSON.
quiz.explain: Create the data inside the handler, then send it with `res.status(201).json(item)`.

quiz.q: A route finished a delete and has nothing to say back. Which call fits best?
quiz.explain: 204 means "No Content": success with an empty body. `res.sendStatus(204)` sets the code and ends the response in one call.

exercise.task:
Add these four routes in `app.js`:

- `GET /api/ping` sends JSON `{ "message": "pong" }`.
- `POST /api/ping` answers with status `201` and JSON `{ "created": true }`.
- `GET /api/secret` answers with status `403` and JSON `{ "error": "Forbidden" }`.
- `DELETE /api/ping` answers with status `204` and no body.

Leave `module.exports = app;` at the bottom.
hints: Use `app.get`, `app.post` and `app.delete` for the three methods. `res.json(...)` sends an object as JSON.
Chain the status before the body: `res.status(201).json(...)`. For the empty answer use `res.sendStatus(204)`.
